monthly_review.summary: You've increased intensity and efficiency this month, trading volume for higher-quality efforts — reflected in faster pace, higher HR, elevated aerobic TE, and improved running economy.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved from 13.28 to 13.44 m/sec per bpm — the largest positive shift across all metrics — indicating better oxygen utilization at given heart rates.

goal_tracker.message: You need 7.6 more km across 2 sessions in the remaining 10 days to match last month’s distance — e.g., one 4.0 km and one 3.6 km run.

insights.title: Improved oxygen economy at submax effort
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.28 to 13.44 m/sec per bpm despite higher average HR (148 vs 142), suggesting better cardiac output coupling and neuromuscular coordination — supported by your 4.0 km run on 2026-04-08 showing 147 spm, 77.92 cm stride, and only 141 bpm.

insights.title: Shift toward threshold and VO2 max work
insights.body: Zone 3+ time jumped from 49% (z3+z4+z5 = 36+12+1) last month to 60% (32+21+7) this month — especially notable in your 2026-04-12 run (163 bpm avg, 4.6 aerobic TE, 90.77 cm stride), which likely spent >20 min in Z4.

insights.title: Stride length variability signals pacing inconsistency
insights.body: Stride length ranged from 70.96 cm (6.2 km @ 9:00/km, 142 bpm) to 90.77 cm (5.0 km @ 7:25/km, 163 bpm) — a 19.8 cm swing — correlating with 21 sec/km pace spread; vertical oscillation remained stable (7.8–8.4 cm), suggesting form breakdown isn’t due to bounce but effort-driven overstriding.

insights.title: Limited low-intensity recovery stimulus
insights.body: Z1 time dropped from 4% to 10% — still critically low — and no run this month had HR <135 bpm or pace >9:30/km; your slowest recent run (2026-04-17, 9:08/km, 144 bpm) was still solidly in Z2, meaning true recovery stimulus is missing.

recommendations.action: Do a 45-min Zone 1 run tomorrow (HR ≤132 bpm, pace ≥9:45/km) with cadence held at 145–148 spm — use your 2026-04-01 run (142 bpm, 9:00/km) as upper HR boundary.
recommendations.reason: Z1 volume is only 10% this month and zero in your last five runs — this will restore parasympathetic tone and reinforce efficient neuromuscular patterning without fatigue.

recommendations.action: Repeat your 2026-04-03 run (5.0 km @ 8:07/km, 149 bpm, 154 spm) on Thursday — same pace, HR target, and cadence — to reinforce consistency in Z3 effort and stride control.
recommendations.reason: That run delivered strong aerobic TE (3.7) with minimal vertical oscillation (8.3 cm) and efficient stride (80.06 cm), making it an ideal repeatable benchmark for sustainable threshold work.

recommendations.action: Add 2x 30-sec strides off the end of Saturday’s run: jog 2 min, accelerate smoothly to ~95% effort over 10 sec, hold for 20 sec at 165–170 bpm and 158–162 spm, then walk 90 sec — repeat x2.
recommendations.reason: Your highest-cadence run (155 spm on 2026-04-01) coincided with lowest HR (142 bpm) and best ground contact (309 ms); strides will reinforce that high-cadence/low-GCT pattern without adding volume.

weekly_focus.description: Prioritize repeatable effort execution — matching pace, HR, cadence, and stride length across similar sessions — to solidify neuromuscular efficiency and improve pacing judgment at all intensities.
suggested_sessions: Zone 1 recovery run (45 min, HR ≤132 bpm)
Threshold repeat (5 km @ 8:07/km, HR 147–151 bpm, cadence 154 spm)
Strides + easy run (6 km total, last 10 min @ 8:45/km with 148–150 spm)
